phwstyle

phwstyle gives the charts, tables, widgets, dashboards, reports and slides you already make one consistent, accessible house style, based on the Public Health Wales visual identity. You bring your own numbers and add one function to style the result. It does not analyse anything.

Installation

phwstyle needs R 4.3 or later and ggplot2 3.5 or later. The Quarto formats need Quarto 1.5 or later. Install it from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Ch3w3y/phwstyle-r", dependencies = TRUE)

dependencies = TRUE also installs the optional packages for every output type. For faster installs, managed computers and installs that fail, see Installation and setup. Run phwstyle::phw_setup_check() once afterwards to see what is ready.

A first chart and a first document

Call use_phw_ggplot() once, then write plain ggplot2:

library(phwstyle)
library(ggplot2)

use_phw_ggplot()   # style every chart in the session

ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~year) +
  labs(title = "Engine size and fuel economy",
       caption = phw_caption("ggplot2::mpg"))

For a document, name a phwstyle format and everything inside it is styled:

output: phwstyle::phw_word_document   # R Markdown
format: phw-typst                     # Quarto, after use_phw_quarto()

What it covers

Output Functions Guide
ggplot2 use_phw_ggplot(), theme_phw(), scale_colour_phw_d() and the other scales, phw_sec_axis(), phw_finalise(), phw_save() Charts
Public health charts phw_epicurve(), phw_pyramid(), phw_funnel(), phw_forest(), phw_spc() Charts
Extensions and several charts phw_style_extensions(), phw_arrange(), phw_title_grob() Charts
Colours and accessibility phw_pal(), phw_colour_key(), phw_default_palette(), phw_check_colours(), phw_cvd(), scale_shape_phw() Colours
Summary tables phw_summary_table(), phw_as_summary(), phw_crosstab(), phw_rate_table(), phw_risk_table(), phw_group_table() Tables
Word, PDF, HTML tables phw_flextable(), phw_gt(), use_phw_gtsummary(), use_phw_flextable() Tables
Maps phw_map(), phw_boundaries(), theme_phw_map(), phw_leaflet(), phw_leaflet_polygons() Maps
Interactive phw_reactable(), phw_datatable(), phw_plotly(), phw_bs_theme(), phw_page_navbar() Interactive
R Markdown and Quarto phw_html_document, phw_word_document, phw_pdf_document, use_phw_quarto() with phw-html, phw-docx, phw-typst, phw-pdf, phw-revealjs, phw-pptx, phw-dashboard Reports, slides and dashboards
Excel and PowerPoint phw_write_xlsx(), phw_pptx() and phw_add_slide() (a 16:9 template), phw_reference_pptx() Excel, PowerPoint and Word
Captions, dates and numbers phw_caption(), phw_date(), phw_number(), phw_percent() Charts
Setup phw_setup_check(), phw_install_fonts(), phw_download_logos() Installation and setup

Getting started walks through one worked example and has a table of which function you need for each task. Anything you add to a plot wins over the defaults, and every word phwstyle writes can be replaced, for example with your own Welsh text.

Gallery

The gallery shows every kind of output with the functions behind it. All examples use made-up data. examples/phwstyle-demo.R builds each output type from one raw data frame.

Accessibility

  • Text colours meet the AA contrast level of the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) on white.
  • The accessible palette stays distinct for colour-blind readers. Turn it on once with use_phw_ggplot(palette = "accessible") and every chart, table and widget uses it. Shape and line type scales add a second cue besides colour.
  • HTML outputs keep a visible keyboard focus outline.

See Colours and accessibility.

Fonts and logos

The Ubuntu typeface is bundled and registered for you. Run phw_install_fonts() once if you use Word, base R graphics or LaTeX on your own computer. The Public Health Wales logo is a trade mark and is not included. Point phwstyle at an approved copy, or run phw_download_logos(). Without a logo, every output is still styled and shows the organisation name. Both are covered in Installation and setup.
